neighbours.label: A statement that something modest is adequate for a stated use ('plenty for', 'good enough for', 'all you need for'), firing around the 'for' or the use; the same objects failing or merely described stay quiet.
fire: For a small office, a single printer is plenty for daily needs.
An old bicycle is good enough for getting to the market.
These budget headphones are more than adequate for casual listening.
A short walk each morning is enough for most older dogs.
For basic photo editing, the free program will do nicely.
A cheap blender is all you really need for making smoothies.
A twenty-liter pack is sufficient for a two-day hike.
The little stove works fine for heating soup on a camping trip.
quiet: In a small office, the single printer jammed again this morning.
An old bicycle leaned against the wall near the market.
These budget headphones broke after a week of casual listening.
A short walk each morning made the older dogs very tired.
The free program crashed during basic photo editing yesterday.
A cheap blender is far too weak for making smoothies.
A twenty-liter pack is much too small for a two-day hike.
The little stove caught fire on our camping trip last year.

notes: The output direction promotes ' enough', ' suffice', ' sufficient'. Near misses keep the object and setting and say it is too weak, broke, or was simply there.
